rawOutput.title: Use the Product Rule Independently
rawOutput.rationale: This problem-solving plan begins with the meaning and procedure of the product rule because you know the power rule but have not encountered this rule. Each 15-minute session keeps one action prominent, starts with a complete example, and then reduces support. Later sessions retrieve and apply the procedure independently.

sessions.title: Understand the product rule
sessions.objective: Recognize when the product rule is needed and understand its two-term structure.
sessions.amountLabel: One rule and one complete worked example
contentTargets: The product rule: (fg)' = f'g + fg'
Identifying the two factors and their derivatives
completionEvidence: Explain why differentiating a product requires two terms
Apply the rule to one example with guided steps

sessions.title: Use the procedure with support
sessions.objective: Differentiate a product by assigning each factor a clear role in the rule.
contentTargets: Substituting f, g, f', and g' into the product rule
completionEvidence: Solve two product-rule problems with step labels
Explain how each resulting term was formed

sessions.title: Choose and apply the rule
sessions.objective: Distinguish products from expressions that only need the power rule, then differentiate correctly.
sessions.amountLabel: One classification set and two derivatives
contentTargets: Recognizing when the product rule applies
Combining the product rule with the power rule
completionEvidence: Classify expressions by whether they require the product rule
Solve two mixed power-rule and product-rule problems

sessions.title: Demonstrate independent use
sessions.objective: Apply the product rule without prompts and repair any error found.
sessions.amountLabel: Three independent problems and one error check
contentTargets: Independent product-rule differentiation
Checking both terms and simplifying the result
completionEvidence: Solve three product-rule derivatives without procedural prompts
Demonstrate an error check by identifying both differentiated-factor terms

essentialIdeas: The product rule says the derivative of a product is the derivative of the first factor times the second, plus the first factor times the derivative of the second.

activities.label: Explain the rule
activities.title: Say it in your own words
activities.body: Write the rule in plain language. Keep it to two sentences.
activities.concept: The product rule says the derivative of a product is the derivative of the first factor times the second, plus the first
activities.correctAnswer: The derivative of a product is the derivative of the first factor times the second, plus the first factor times the derivative of the second.
activities.feedback: A complete response names both terms and shows that each factor gets differentiated once. If one factor is missing from a term, repair that part.

activities.label: Fix the missing term
activities.title: Correct the rule
activities.body: Revise your explanation if needed. Make sure both parts of the rule appear.
activities.misconceptionSummary: Leaving out one of the two terms in the product rule.
activities.concept: The product rule says the derivative of a product is the derivative of the first factor times the second, plus the first
activities.correctAnswer: The derivative of a product is the derivative of the first factor times the second, plus the first factor times the derivative of the second.
activities.feedback: The repair is complete when both terms are present and each factor is differentiated in exactly one term.

activities.label: Explain again
activities.title: Restate the rule clearly
activities.body: Give the rule again from memory. Do not copy the earlier wording.
activities.concept: The product rule says the derivative of a product is the derivative of the first factor times the second, plus the first
activities.correctAnswer: The derivative of a product is the derivative of the first factor times the second, plus the first factor times the derivative of the second.
activities.feedback: Success means the rule is accurate, complete, and stated without copying the model.

activities.label: Recognize the rule
activities.title: Which rule fits here?
activities.body: Choose the correct differentiation rule for a product expression.
choices: Use the product rule: differentiate one factor, keep the other, then add the reverse term.
Differentiate each factor and multiply the answers.
Subtract the derivative of the second factor from the first factor.
activities.correctAnswer: Use the product rule: differentiate one factor, keep the other, then add the reverse term.
activities.feedback: A product needs two terms in the derivative, one for each factor getting its turn. The other choices miss that structure.
